question: Do the three regime-independent results (exact LSI programs, harmonic failure of deep networks, anti-aliasing as a weight edit) and the compression-regime price survive at 256 x 256 (weights / pixels 0.03-0.5) on standard natural-image test sets, and does the exact program algebra help weight-space learning once the zoo is large enough for a permutation-equivariant classifier to fit?

A_natural_256.data: Kodak (24 images, 768 x 512) and, if present, DIV2K validation 0801-0900 as 256 x 256 grey crops (centre and quarter-offset, std > 0.08); n = 24 crops for the main table, n = 48 for the two cheapest zoos (sensitivity).

bounded: deep_h128_swing4 (2-128-128-1, swing bound 2 and 4, PyTorch projection)

A_natural_256.recipe: 3,000 Adam steps at 1e-3, omega 30, PyTorch trainer on GPU; function-space references 4x supersampled; anti-aliased x4 downsampling as in stage 08.

predictions_frozen_before_running.S1_gap_persists: At every matched pair the deep network exceeds the shallow one by at least 3 dB and at most 12 dB median PSNR.
predictions_frozen_before_running.S2_gap_not_growing_with_compression: The 4k-pair gap at 256 x 256 (ratio 0.07) is not larger than the 128 x 128 gap of the same pair (9.5 dB) plus 1 dB.
predictions_frozen_before_running.S3_absolute_range: deep_h128x3 median PSNR lies between 26 and 36 dB; deep_h64 between 21 and 30 dB; shallow_w1024 between 15 and 23 dB.
predictions_frozen_before_running.S4_harmonic_regime: Every unbounded deep zoo has median harmonic index H >= 6 and first-order blur ratio >= 0.7.
predictions_frozen_before_running.S5_exactness: On every shallow zoo the Gaussian and box programs have function-space MSE below 1e-4 x no-edit MSE on every crop, and the anti-aliasing program (1 spp) beats 4 x 4 supersampling (16 spp) by at least 15 dB median.

predictions_frozen_before_running.S7_width_saturates: Within the shallow family, each doubling of width gains at most 1.0 dB median PSNR at 256 x 256.

B_weight_space_augmentation.models: own NP/HNP NFN classifier (wsinr/nfn_layers.py, c = 64 and 128), DeepSets2 and aligned MLP as references; 3 seeds; n_train in {1000, 2000, 5000, 10000}; augmentation none / programs (exact translation, flip, rotation, zoom, contrast, brightness) / permute.

predictions_frozen_before_running.W1_capacity: NFN c=128 with no augmentation reaches at least 60 % test accuracy at n = 10,000 (otherwise the classifier, not the augmentation, is the bottleneck and W2-W4 are void).
predictions_frozen_before_running.W2_programs_help_small_n: At n = 1,000 the programs augmentation beats none by at least 2.0 points (mean of 3 seeds) for the NFN.
predictions_frozen_before_running.W3_programs_help_large_n: At n = 10,000 the programs augmentation beats none by at least 0.5 points for the NFN.
predictions_frozen_before_running.W4_programs_vs_permute: Programs are at least as good as permutation augmentation at every n for the NFN (permutation is a symmetry the NFN already has, so it should add nothing).
